EASY_PAGES.footer: Plain triads only — no 7ths, 9ths, or slash chords. Good starting point if you're newer to this.

EASY_PAGES.note: One chord per bar. Plain triads, root position.

EASY_PAGES.title: EASY — 50S TURNAROUND (I–vi–IV–V)
EASY_PAGES.note: Straight quarter notes, one chord per bar. Try singing along — it fits almost anything.
EASY_PAGES.footer: Plain triads only — no 7ths, 9ths, or slash chords. Good starting point if you're newer to this.

TECHNIQUE_PAGES.title: BLOCK CHORDS vs. BROKEN CHORDS
TECHNIQUE_PAGES.subtitle: same notes, two different feelings
bullets: BLOCK CHORD — play every RH note at the same time. This is the default in every page of this book.
BROKEN CHORD (ARPEGGIO) — play the same notes one at a time instead of together, usually low to high.
Breaking a chord turns a stab of harmony into a flowing line — good for intros, ballads, and quiet sections.
No new notes needed. Any RH voicing already printed in this book can be broken exactly as written.
TECHNIQUE_PAGES.tryIntro: Cmaj7 from LATE-NIGHT MELT (page {page}) — RH: G - B - C - E, LH: C
trySteps: BLOCK — play G, B, C, E together over LH C.
BROKEN (UP) — play C, E, G, B one at a time, low to high, holding pedal through all four.
BROKEN (UP-DOWN) — play C, E, G, B, G, E, C, then move to the next chord.

TECHNIQUE_PAGES.title: INVERSIONS & SMOOTH VOICE LEADING
TECHNIQUE_PAGES.subtitle: why the RH notes almost never start on the root
bullets: An inversion is the same chord with a different note on the bottom — Cmaj7 can be C-E-G-B, E-G-B-C, G-B-C-E, or B-C-E-G. Same four notes, different order.
Every RH voicing in this book was chosen for smooth voice leading: whichever inversion keeps the most notes in common with the chord before it, so your hand barely has to move.
When you build your own progression, look for the inversion where the fewest fingers change position between chords — that's what makes a progression feel connected instead of jumpy.
TECHNIQUE_PAGES.tryIntro: Am7 → Cmaj7, both from LATE-NIGHT MELT (page {page})
trySteps: Am7 = A - C - E - G.  Cmaj7 = C - E - G - B.
Three notes (C, E, G) are shared between them — only one finger has to move, from A to B.
Play both chords back to back and notice how little your hand shifts. That's the whole trick.

TECHNIQUE_PAGES.title: LEFT-HAND BASS PATTERNS
TECHNIQUE_PAGES.subtitle: the LH note printed in this book is just a starting point
bullets: SINGLE NOTE — exactly what's printed: one sustained bass note per chord. Calm and simple.
OCTAVE — play the LH note together with the same note an octave higher, or alternate between them. Fuller, more pop/rock.
OPEN FIFTH — play the LH note together with the note a fifth above it (e.g. C + G). Open and powerful — a little rock, a little gospel.
WALKING BASS — instead of jumping straight to the next chord's root, fill the gap with one or two passing notes on the way there. Jazzier, more forward motion.
TECHNIQUE_PAGES.tryIntro: BIG POP EMOTION, Loop A (page {page}) — C, G, Am, F
trySteps: SINGLE — LH: C, G, A, F.
OCTAVE — LH: C+C', G+G', A+A', F+F' (each note doubled an octave up).
OPEN FIFTH — LH: C+G, G+D, A+E, F+C.
WALKING (C to G) — LH: C, D, E, G — then keep connecting each chord to the next the same way.

TECHNIQUE_PAGES.title: PEDALING TECHNIQUES
TECHNIQUE_PAGES.subtitle: the pedal is a mixing tool, not an on/off switch
bullets: DIRECT PEDALING — press the pedal down at the same moment you play the chord. This is the book's default whenever a page says “change pedal with the harmony.”

LEGATO (SYNCOPATED) PEDALING — lift the pedal right as your fingers land on the new chord, then press back down a fraction of a second later. Removes the clash between old and new harmony while still gluing the two chords together.
HALF-PEDALING — release the pedal only partway instead of fully. Thins out the sustain without cutting it dead — useful anywhere a page says to “let edges blur” without turning to mud.
TECHNIQUE_PAGES.tryIntro: QUIET HYMN, Loop A (page {page}) — F, Bb, F, C7
trySteps: First pass: direct pedaling — press down with each new chord, release fully before the next.
Second pass: legato pedaling on the same four chords — lift right as you play, press back a beat later.
Notice how much smoother the join feels on the second pass.

TECHNIQUE_PAGES.title: COMPING RHYTHMS
TECHNIQUE_PAGES.subtitle: one chord can be played a dozen different ways rhythmically
bullets: STRAIGHT HOLD — play the chord once and let it ring for the full bar. What most “playing note” instructions in this book assume by default.
BACKBEAT PULSE — restrike the same chord softly on beats 2 and 4 instead of just holding it. Adds a pop/rock feel without changing a single note.
SYNCOPATED PUSH — play the next chord an eighth note early, right before the beat it “belongs” to. Adds forward energy, common in R&B and gospel.
BROKEN-CHORD PULSE — instead of holding the block chord, arpeggiate it in steady rhythm (see the Block vs. Broken page) so the chord itself becomes the rhythm part.
TECHNIQUE_PAGES.tryIntro: WARM & HOPEFUL, Loop A (page {page}) — G, D/F#, Em7, Cadd9
trySteps: Play the same four chords four ways: straight hold, backbeat pulse, syncopated push, broken-chord pulse.
Same notes every time — only the rhythm changes the feeling.

TECHNIQUE_PAGES.title: TOPPING CHORDS WITH A SIMPLE MELODY
TECHNIQUE_PAGES.subtitle: let one finger sing a tune while the rest of the hand holds still
bullets: Once a loop feels automatic, stop thinking of the RH as one block. Let your pinky (the top note) move to a nearby scale tone while the other fingers hold their notes — that top note becomes a simple melody.
The reverse works too: keep the top notes still and let the thumb-side note move underneath them for a countermelody in the middle of the texture.
You don't have to invent a melody from scratch — look at how the top note already changes from chord to chord. Most progressions in this book already have one hiding in plain sight.
TECHNIQUE_PAGES.tryIntro: DREAMY / FLOATING, Loop A (page {page}) — Ebmaj7, Bb/D, Cm9, Abmaj9
trySteps: Top notes in order: Eb, D, Eb, Eb — that's already a tiny melody.
Play that top note slightly louder than the rest of the chord and let it lead.

MORE_PROGRESSIONS.title: 12-BAR BLUES
MORE_PROGRESSIONS.note: Swing the eighth notes (long-short, not straight) and let the LH walk — this is a shuffle, not a straight quarter-note groove.
MORE_PROGRESSIONS.footer: The classic I7-IV7-V7 blues form — 12 bars, then loop right back to bar 1.

MORE_PROGRESSIONS.title: ANDALUSIAN CADENCE
MORE_PROGRESSIONS.note: Play it as rolled (broken) chords on every beat, and speed up slightly as you descend — like a flamenco guitarist building tension.
MORE_PROGRESSIONS.footer: i – VII – VI – V, the descending minor pattern behind flamenco, ‘Hit the Road Jack,’ and countless film cues.

MORE_PROGRESSIONS.title: ii-V-I JAZZ TURNAROUND
MORE_PROGRESSIONS.note: Swing feel. The ii and V chords share several notes — keep your hand still and let only what has to move, move (see Inversions, page {tech_page}).
MORE_PROGRESSIONS.footer: ii–V–I is the single most common move in jazz — learn it in one key and the other eleven come almost for free.

MORE_PROGRESSIONS.title: CIRCLE-OF-FIFTHS SEQUENCE
MORE_PROGRESSIONS.note: Use a metronome, one chord per beat. This is a hand-position drill, not a mood — don't stop to think, just move.
MORE_PROGRESSIONS.footer: All 12 major keys, descending in fifths, then back to C. Try it in reverse (ascending fifths) once this feels automatic.

KEYBOARD
PROGRESSION BOOK
SECOND EDITION · POCKET VIEW
Sit down. Pick a page. Start playing.
Every page is self-contained — RH notes and LH bass side by side.
3 EASY + 6 TECHNIQUES + 4 MORE PROGRESSIONS
+ 20 MOOD LOOPS + 10 SONG VIBES
frontMatterSource.renderHowTo:
HOW TO USE IT
No required order. On every chord line, LH (left hand / bass note) sits right next to RH (right hand notes, played together unless you arpeggiate them). Change pedal with the harmony unless a page says otherwise.
Tap Contents above to jump to any section, or swipe / use Prev·Next to move through the whole book in order.
frontMatterSource.renderDivider:
FAVORITE
SONG VIBES
Familiar harmonic worlds reduced to something you can sit down and play.
These are simplified chord/vibe sketches rather than full transcriptions.
frontMatterSource.renderKeepPlaying:
KEEP PLAYING
If one loop grabs you, stay there. Change the rhythm. Move the bass an octave. Break the RH apart. Or do absolutely nothing to it and just enjoy the sound.
